Quick notes inline: 
- Control plane: The minimal control-plane signals required for rollout and health-checks are (1) config sync API, (2) model version manifest fetch, and (3) rollout control webhook. BayCorp can choose to host a control agent in their VPC that proxies these calls to Redwood control endpoints over a customer-managed egress path.
- Data plane: Inference nodes perform two types of outbound connections: initial model fetch (s3-compatible or artifact proxy) and runtime telemetry (metrics/logs). For low-risk environments we recommend pinned artifact endpoints via private egress; for stricter SOC requirements we support pulling artifacts via a pre-provisioned airgap bundle.

Adding a couple of operational points so Harper has them ahead of the readout: 

- Egress bucket / artifact endpoints: we can sign short-lived URLs for artifacts and optionally let BayCorp route them through their artifact proxy (recommended). That eliminates the need for open wildcard egress to public S3.
- KV cache replication: if you run a cache-populated inference fleet, we recommend an internal tier for warm-up traffic and a small outbound-only channel for cache miss fetches. We can show traffic diagrams.
- Control-plane heartbeat: control agents use an HTTPS POST to our control endpoint on port 443. If BayCorp requires a private peering-only path, we can negotiate a private endpoint via a marketplace/private-connector (this is heavier lift and part of Dedicated/Private enterprise plans).

Harper — good questions, quick answers ahead of the readout: 

1) Presigned internal URLs: Yes. Our runtime accepts presigned artifact URLs that resolve on customer internal DNS as long as the control agent can validate a signed token. We will share a short spec for the token exchange (attached as part of the reference diagram bundle). For airgapped customers we also support an encrypted model bundle you scp into the node.

2) Telemetry: We support metrics-only mode for customers who insist on no log/traces egress. Metrics use a Prometheus-compatible pushgateway pattern or remote write; logs/traces can be kept local and optionally collected by a customer-side logging forwarder. We'll document required metric names and cardinality budget.
